decision.reason: The complete four-page BFH III R24/12 judgment (11 April 2013, paragraphs1–26), body SHA-256 8f914fd2ee4844996197b164ae9f9b1f90f7989bad146c75aa18a1c116fdb605, concerns the historical2006–2008 income-and-receipts regime. Paragraph24 expressly gives nonbinding remand guidance permitting SvEV values to estimate benefits in kind, subject to differing individual values. DA-KG2025 A19.6(1) sentence3, body SHA-256 3a37dc324efe185099d379748b01ab401ccbe15cfaa0a5b60c37c39183eb8998, expressly retains that option when individual evidence cannot be provided. This valuation option bears on disability-related means under EStG32(4), A19.4–A19.6 and qualifying_child_count; it remains unencoded. Do not import the historical7680EUR ceiling or former section32/70 framework into2025. Paragraphs18–22 reject presumed half-sharing for unmarried parents; the separate married/registered-partner rule in A19.6(2) does not extend it to unmarried couples. Both discovery identities must ultimately bind one canonical judgment module; neither duplicate discovery nor the guidance citation supplies executable coverage. Full source binding and review: in-kind-support-estimation-source-review.json. Exact BStBlII issue/page verification remains separate.
